solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Great buggy with unspecified amount in fuel tank

indicators.note: in says the unspecified amount is placed inside the jumbled letters
buggy, in the sense of full of faults or crazy, tells us the letters of the preceding word are jumbled

explanation.surface: A great big vehicle carries an unknown quantity of fuel in its tank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buggy' looks like a noun (a vehicle) but is the anagram signal, and 'fuel tank' is the whole definition: a holder for town gas.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas holder storing town gas for supply is a large tank of fuel.

clue.text: Arise and go for followers?

parts.note: the answer means arise, and it is what precedes 'and go' in the phrase for energy, so 'and go' are its followers

explanation.definitionFit: To stand up from bed or a chair is to arise, a plain phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Star has depressing experience with drink

explanation.surface: A celebrity has a bad time and reaches for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A sundowner is an alcoholic drink taken at sunset.

clue.text: Significant base in Gulf with promotion for leader of force

parts.note: base, meaning low or ignoble, is mean

indicators.text: with promotion for leader of force
indicators.note: promotion lifts the first letter of force higher up the word, which in a down entry means nearer the top

explanation.surface: An important military base in the Gulf, with a promotion for the commanding officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader of force' is F; promoting it moves it up GULF to give GFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something meaningful carries real significance, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Beef for league leaders?

definitions.meaning: a lean cut of beef from the upper leg
the team at the head of a league table is the side on top

explanation.walkthrough: TOPSIDE is a British name for a lean joint of beef; the '?' flags the playful split into TOP SIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Topside is a British cut of beef, and read as two words it describes the top team.

clue.text: Was king reportedly kept in check?

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is as heard, a sound-alike of another

parts.note: a horse kept in check is reined

explanation.surface: Was the monarch, so they say, restrained?
explanation.definitionFit: A king on the throne reigned, the verb for a monarch's rule.

clue.text: Orthodox Jew may be identified

parts.note: one who may be identified has some form of identity

explanation.surface: A religious man might be recognised.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole phrase 'may be identified' reads as HAS ID: someone with identification on them.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hasid is a member of a strictly observant Orthodox Jewish movement.

clue.text: Eyecatching pirate?

definitions.meaning: in a ...-and-eye fastening, the curved metal part catches the eye
Captain of the Jolly Roger in Peter Pan

explanation.walkthrough: 'Eyecatching' reads as striking, but it is literal: the part of a clasp that catches an eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Hook is a fictional pirate, and in a hook-and-eye fastening the curved part catches the eye.

clue.text: That woman will appear shortly in a magazine article

explanation.surface: A female writer will soon feature in a glossy publication.
explanation.walkthrough: The magazine is not a periodical but the chamber of a gun; the article it holds is ammunition.
explanation.definitionFit: A shell is a piece of ammunition loaded into a gun's magazine.

clue.text: Idle dogs don't start moving from original position

indicators.note: moving says the letters of the preceding words change places
start picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Lazy dogs do not get up and move around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges IDLEDOGS to DISLODGE, and 'start' adds D from don't; 'moving' also colours the definition, as the setter intends.
explanation.definitionFit: Dislodged describes something knocked out of the place it started in.

clue.text: Country where native originally appears in classic garb

indicators.note: appears in tells us one piece shows up inside the other

parts.note: the toga was the garment of classical Rome

indicators.note: originally picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A nation where a local first turns up in traditional dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonga is a Pacific island country.

clue.text: Synthetic resin: pros and cons

indicators.note: synthetic means artificially made up, so the letters are put together anew

explanation.surface: A note on plastic resin listing its advantages and disadvantages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pros and cons' looks like a set phrase, but 'pros' is fodder and 'cons' alone is the definition, in the sense of convicts.
explanation.definitionFit: Cons is slang for convicts, people serving prison sentences.

clue.text: Writing mostly about seeing food

indicators.note: about means the trimmed word goes around the next piece
mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: vision is the faculty of seeing

explanation.surface: Most of a piece of writing is about spotting something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims PROSE to PROS, which goes 'about' VISION.
explanation.definitionFit: Provisions are supplies of food and drink.

clue.text: Too revolutionary a part for Yugoslavia

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the stretch is read backwards
a part for means only a stretch of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A rebel taking a role in the Balkans as well.
explanation.walkthrough: The run OSLA inside Yugoslavia, read backwards, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Also and too are synonyms meaning in addition.

clue.text: Incredible captain's heart is in a measure taken at sea

indicators.note: is in tells us that letter sits inside the following phrase

parts.note: a sounding is a measurement of water depth

indicators.note: heart picks the middle letter of the word captain

explanation.surface: Amazingly, the ship's master is busy checking the depth of water.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of CAPTAIN is T, put inside A SOUNDING after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Astounding means astonishing, so hard to believe.

clue.text: Welsh sticker left out by Descartes

indicators.note: by means set beside the philosopher's name
out means that letter is removed

explanation.surface: A Welsh adhesive left behind by a French philosopher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Welsh' is the verb meaning go back on a deal, not the nationality. RENEGUE is a variant spelling of renege.
explanation.definitionFit: To welsh on a bet is to fail to honour it, which is to renege.

clue.text: Trustworthy salesman on university board

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: A reliable sales rep sits on a university's governing body.
explanation.definitionFit: A reputable firm has a good name and can be trusted.

clue.text: Spiffy sprinter's forte

definitions.meaning: a sprinter excels at running fast in short bursts

explanation.definitionFit: Dashing means stylishly smart, and dashing is also what a sprinter does best.

clue.text: Pantheist reformed once

indicators.note: reformed means the letters are put into a new form

explanation.surface: A believer in nature-gods changed his ways at one time.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means formerly, at some earlier time.

clue.text: Bother with fresh book about ancient city

indicators.note: about means the first pieces go around the city

parts.note: Ur was an ancient Sumerian city

explanation.surface: Trouble over a new book on an old city.
explanation.definitionFit: To perturb someone is to unsettle or bother them.

clue.text: Endless barbecue arranged for young carnivore

indicators.note: arranged means the remaining letters are put in a new order
endless means the final letter of the word is cut off

explanation.surface: A never-ending cookout laid on for a young meat-eater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' drops the last E of barbecue, and 'arranged' shuffles BARBECU.
explanation.definitionFit: A young bear is a carnivore, being a member of the order Carnivora.

clue.text: A debtor having settlement cancelled

indicators.note: settlement suggests the letters are settled into a new order

explanation.surface: A borrower's agreed payment plan is called off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' is a link word; 'settlement' rearranges A DEBTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An aborted plan is one called off before completion.

clue.text: Essayist is working with a theologian

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, denotes a theologian

explanation.surface: A writer busy alongside a religious scholar.
explanation.walkthrough: Joseph Addison was an English essayist of the early 18th century.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Addison, co-founder of The Spectator, is a famous essayist.

clue.text: Rabbit in hospital kitchen

indicators.note: in signals the answer sits inside the following words

explanation.surface: A bunny is kept in a hospital's kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit' is British slang: to rabbit on is to chatter at length.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to rabbit means to talk on and on.

clue.text: Top copper standing in — is that clear?

indicators.note: in means the reversed metal goes inside the top
standing, in a down entry, turns the word upright, so read upwards

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A senior police officer is filling in: is that understood?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top copper' looks like a senior police officer, but Top is LID and copper is CU, which 'standing' turns into UC.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucid means clear and easily understood.

clue.text: First and principal town on the Thames

parts.note: a maiden voyage is a first one
the head is the principal person

explanation.surface: The leading town on the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Maidenhead is a Berkshire town on the River Thames, west of London.

clue.text: Frightful old man about to be imprisoned

indicators.note: to be imprisoned means the next piece is held within the father

parts.note: old man is slang for father, dad

explanation.surface: A fearsome father is about to be jailed.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread as an adjective means dreadful or causing fear.

clue.text: Box not entirely free

indicators.note: not entirely means the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A container that is not quite empty.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to box, especially in practice.

clue.text: Sponsor group's tours?

parts.note: a pack is a group, and the 's stands for 'is' to make the plural

explanation.surface: A sponsor's group goes on tour.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb sense: she backpacks means she tours with a rucksack; the '?' flags it.
explanation.definitionFit: To backpack is to travel around carrying a rucksack, a budget form of touring.

clue.text: Wild creature that is caged

indicators.note: caged means one piece is shut inside the other

explanation.surface: A creature in a cage goes wild.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild with anger is irate.

clue.text: Bush, a sort of statesman

definitions.meaning: a shrub bearing white flowers and dark berries
an ... statesman is a senior, respected figure

explanation.definitionFit: The elder is a shrub, and an elder statesman is a respected veteran politician.

clue.text: Ignorant about the big end

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone ignorant about the big end of a car engine.
explanation.definitionFit: Benighted means in intellectual or moral darkness, so ignorant.
